_what_this_is: What the Zenodo record at `published_doi` ACTUALLY CONTAINS, as published, plus any version that has been DRAFTED but not yet published. Not what the repository contains now — that is fusion-junction-aso-archive-manifest.json, which moves with every commit. This file moves only when a version is drafted or published on Zenodo, and publishing is an irreversible act the author performs by hand.
_why_this_exists: Round 15, 2026-08-22. Three independent reviewers found the same defect from three directions: the submitted manuscript's Data and code availability says 'the archived copy is the citable one', and the archived copy was 16 files behind the repository — including the extended report itself, whose deposited text still carried two statements this repository had since corrected (the void-test definition, and a claim that the dinucleotide-preserving scramble holds the 5' guanine run). It shipped unnoticed because NOTHING RECORDED WHAT WAS DEPOSITED. `--check-archive` compares the manifest to the working tree, so it turns green exactly as the tree walks away from the deposit, and `archive_content_digest` is stored only inside the manifest that computes it, so it can never disagree with itself.
_the_window_this_file_exists_to_make_leg: Between drafting a corrected version and publishing it, the papers cite a DOI that is not yet live and the published record is still the old one. That gap is deliberate and is the whole point of the reserve-then-rebuild ordering: the manuscript must print the identifier the archive will carry BEFORE the files are frozen, because a published version cannot be edited. `pending` records the drafted version so the gap is a stated state rather than a disagreement nobody can see.
_how_to_update: When the pending version is PUBLISHED: move its doi/digest/n_files/git_revision up into `published`, set `published.published` to the date, and delete `pending`. When a new version is DRAFTED: set `pending`. AND READ THE RECORD BACK BEFORE WRITING `published` — `record=verify` on deposit-zenodo.yml does it with no token. 'Somebody clicked publish' is a report about an outside system; 'the DOI printed in the papers resolves to a published record' is a reading, and this repository has already paid three days for the difference (the bioRxiv status that stayed ⏳ after the rejection). NEVER edit either block to silence a gate — the gate is the whole point, and a green gate on a stale deposit is what this file was created to end.

pending._why_this_version_exists: ⛔ THE PUBLISHED ARCHIVE HAD DRIFTED 55 FILES BEHIND THE PAPERS, AND THE DRIFT WAS IN THE OVERCLAIMING DIRECTION. Measured 2026-08-29 by diffing the manifest's own 483-path inventory between the published record's git_revision (091721519) and HEAD. The deposited extended report still read 'both are invisible to a screen that ranks candidates by global identity' and 'a contiguous run of eleven or twelve base pairs inside a 16-mer leaves five or four positions unpaired'; the repository had since corrected those to 'mostly but not wholly blind' and 'positions outside that run — which are not all unpaired', each with its recomputation. The journal article, the tables, the sequences CSV and all three figures had moved too. A reader following the cited DOI would have got artefacts making STRONGER claims than the paper citing them — round 15's defect (`_why_this_exists`) recurring. ⚠ AND `--check-archive` CANNOT CATCH IT: it compares the manifest to the WORKING TREE, so it goes green exactly as the tree walks away from the deposit. What caught it was diffing the inventory against the published record's own git_revision.
pending._what_remains: Publishing, by hand, on Zenodo — https://zenodo.org/deposit/22166420. Irreversible, and trimcrae's act. ⛔ AND IT IS THE FIRST OF TWO, IN THIS ORDER: the Qeios v2 post is the second and must come AFTER, because v2's Data availability cites this DOI and a reader who follows it before publication gets nothing. Until then the papers cite a DOI that does not yet resolve, which is the reserve-then-rebuild ordering working as designed rather than a defect.

published._what_the_concept_doi_is_for: Zenodo's per-RECORD identifier, which always resolves to the NEWEST version. It is recorded here because it is a fact this repository did not have until the record was read, and because the question of whether a paper should cite it has an answer: NO. A manuscript's Data availability must name a FROZEN version, or the archive it promises changes under the reader every time a correction is deposited. Both papers cite the version DOI above and must go on doing so. The concept DOI is for a reader who wants 'all versions', and for nothing in the manuscripts.
